column1: # The classification table: what a tool call was for, decided by pattern.
# Format: class<TAB>family<TAB>rule
#   class   one of the router's classes (see `Class::ALL`)
#   family  the tool family the rule applies to: shell, read, edit, glob,
#           grep, web, list -- the tool NAME is mapped to a family by the
#           `FAMILIES` table in router/mod.rs, because harnesses name the
#           same tool differently and the corpus pins the names seen
#   rule    a conjunction of `key=value` terms, space-separated:
#             word=a|b     the last simple command's first word (basename)
#             sub=a|b      the subcommand: the first operand that is not a
#                          flag. Position matters -- a term that took any
#                          operand would read `cargo build --features test`
#                          as a test run
#             flag=x|y     any operand starts with `-x`, or is `--x`,
#                          for one of these
#             ext=a|b      any operand path (or the read tool's path) has
#                          one of these extensions
#             *            matches anything of the family
# Rows are tried in order; the first row whose family and every term match
# wins. A call matching no row is `unknown`, which routes to the declared
# default -- a fork with the generic ask -- and emits an unclassified event.
# Silence is never the default: the 53% of steps that were inert were inert
# by class, not by absence from this table.
# Order is load-bearing, so a row that an earlier row already claims can
# never fire. `no_row_of_the_table_can_ever_fire_from_below_an_earlier_one`
# refuses such a row: two of them sat here unreachable behind the
# side-effect row, and `npm test` was deferred to the turn boundary instead
# of being asked for its outcome.
# Document versus source is decided by extension, and the document set is
# the small one: everything not listed is source, because a reader that
# defaulted to "document" would route every unfamiliar file extension to the
# finding ask instead of the api-surface ask.
# --- listings and probes: inert, no fork ---
directory-listing

directory-listing
inert
# `sed -i` rewrites the file it is pointed at, and `sed -n 80,160p` reads it.
# The row sits above the reads because rows are tried in order and the read
# row names `sed` too: an in-place edit read as a read is a turn whose change
# nothing recorded. Both spellings of the flag: `sed --in-place` rewrote the
# file just as `sed -i` did, and was read as a read.
edit
